title: Water levels in 299 minimally pumped US wells rose faster than they fell at 1-24 month lags; monthly rain-driven and linear store models gave at most half of the 12-month asymmetry
abstract: Question: sci:bd955a4f found that GRACE land water storage rises faster than it falls (skewness g(12) = 0.099 of 12-month changes), and named pumping, lakes and nonlinear recharge as untested causes. Does the same time asymmetry occur in natural water tables, and do rain-driven store models reproduce it? Data: USGS NWIS daily water levels of 299 wells of the USGS Groundwater Climate Response Network (CRN; wells selected for minimal pumping effect), 15 years or more each within 1980-2026; NOAA nClimDiv division precipitation and temperature. Method: per well, linear trend and seasonal harmonics removed; g(L) = skewness of x(t+L) - x(t), L = 1-24 months; network mean of 79 blocks of 2 degrees; block sign-flip test and 200 IAAFT surrogates per well. Linear ARX, sign-split and soil-bucket recharge stores were fitted per well, simulated with the observed forcing and processed like the data. Results: g was positive at all lags: 0.90 at L = 1, 0.29 at L = 12 (95% CI 0.19-0.40; IAAFT null -0.054 to 0.055; sign-flip p = 5e-5) and 0.18 at L = 24. It was robust to a quadratic trend (0.27) and to the 2002-2026 window (0.25). It was larger in dry divisions (arid g(12) = 0.88, 10 wells; humid 0.16, 142 wells; dry minus humid +0.67, CI 0.30-1.05) and increased with depth to water (Spearman 0.18, p = 0.002). GRACE TWS in the 61 cells that contain the wells gave g(12) = -0.003. Models with noise gave g(12) = 0.037-0.062 against an observed 0.30 (difference 0.23-0.25, CIs exclude 0). Noise-free runs gave at most 0.13 (soil bucket), which also matched g(1). Exploratory level-dependent drainage (0.060) and forcing-free AR(24) with resampled residuals (0.049) also failed; a synthetic control showed that the AR check recovers 66% of a known asymmetry. Conclusion: natural water tables rise fast and fall slowly over months to years without pumping. Monthly linear, sign-split, hinge and soil-bucket stores driven by regional rain give at most half of the 6-24 month asymmetry. The larger effect at deep water tables and in dry climates agrees with episodic recharge, which these monthly models do not represent. Point water-table asymmetry does not appear in GRACE at the same places. Limitations: division rain is smoother than rain at a well; no daily or focused-recharge models were tested; only 12 wells are in dry divisions; single-well tests have low power at long lags; the model variants, AR checks and GRACE comparison are partly exploratory.
